results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the VFB database. VFB records show that the mushroom body is divided into these three parts, with the calyx receiving sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus being a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes, and the mushroom body lobe system consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch. VFB holds various records related to the mushroom body, including [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body, and [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of mushroom body") subclasses of the mushroom body, which may provide further information on its structure and organization.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response: The adult Drosophila brain contains several types of Kenyon cells. VFB records show that there are subclasses of [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), including [[KCab-c](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110929 "Open KCab-c in Virtual Fly Brain")(i)](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049111 "Open KCab-c(i) in Virtual Fly Brain"), KCab-c, [KCg-m](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111061 "Open KCg-m in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Kenyon cell of main calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047926 "Open Kenyon cell of main calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). Additionally, the data indicates that Kenyon cells can be classified into alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into subtypes. VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") records of subclasses of Kenyon cell, providing evidence of the diversity of Kenyon cell types. To explore the different types of Kenyon cells further, you can use VFB to list all available images of Kenyon cell, which currently holds [31468](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of Kenyon cell") records, or examine the scRNAseq data for Kenyon cell, which has [79](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,anatScRNAseqQuery "Run in VFB: scRNAseq data for Kenyon cell") records.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are not explicitly stated in the provided evidence. However, VFB holds data on neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, with [367](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") records annotated. These neurons are likely to be the main input neurons to the mushroom body, as they form synapses within it. VFB also holds data on tracts/nerves innervating the mushroom body, with [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,TractsNervesInnervatingHere "Run in VFB: Tracts/nerves innervating mushroom body") records annotated, which may provide further information on the input neurons. Additionally, VFB has annotated [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ExpressionOverlapsHere "Run in VFB: Expression patterns overlapping mushroom body") expression patterns overlapping the mushroom body, which could be relevant to understanding the inputs to this brain region. To determine the specific input neurons, further queries can be made using VFB's data on neurons with presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body and tracts/nerves innervating the mushroom body.

results.response: The primary neurotransmitter used by mushroom body Kenyon cells is acetylcholine, as indicated by VFB neurotransmitter tags. VFB holds various data related to [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), including a large number of images, subclasses, scRNAseq data, transgene expression data, and downstream and upstream connectivity classes. results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to the mushroom body and lateral horn, as indicated by the information from VFB. Specifically, antennal lobe projection neurons send synaptic output to the mushroom body calyx and/or lateral horn. VFB holds numerous records related to the antennal lobe, including neurons with some part in the antennal lobe, neurons with synaptic terminals in the antennal lobe, and tracts/nerves innervating the antennal lobe. To explore the connections of the antennal lobe in more detail, you can examine the available images of the antennal lobe, or investigate the specific neurons with presynaptic or postsynaptic terminals in the antennal lobe.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
VFB has annotated [9413](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047887,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central brain") neuron types with some part in the [adult central brain](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047887 "Open adult central brain in Virtual Fly Brain"). The connectome data indicates that there are more than 125,000 neurons, but this is not a count specific to the adult central brain. VFB does not currently hold a specific published biological total for the number of neurons in the adult central brain, but it has annotated 9413 neuron types in this region.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- more than 125,000 neurons (adult Drosophila central brain connectome/model) — A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing. — PMID 39358519
- ~139,255 neurons (whole adult Drosophila brain) — Neuronal wiring diagram of an adult brain. — PMID 39358518

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response:
The main components of the Drosophila central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the noduli, and the protocerebral bridge. The literature (Buchanan and Laurent, 1998; Young and Armstrong, 2010; Wolff et al., 2015; Heinze and Homberg, 2007) suggests that these components are associated with functions such as spatial memory, visual navigation, and the integration of sensory information. 

VFB does not currently hold specific data on the functions associated with each component of the Drosophila central complex. However, it may hold data on the neuroanatomy of the central complex and its constituent parts, which could be used to inform queries about the relationships between these components and their associated functions. 

Follow-up queries could include exploring the neuroanatomical structure of the central complex components, examining the connectivity between these components and other brain regions, or investigating the expression of specific genes or proteins within these components.

However, the specific connections between types of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neurons and types of MBONs are not detailed here. VFB has annotated subclasses of MBON ([69](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of MBON") records) and subclasses of [adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049839 "Open adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") ([21](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00049839,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron") records), which may be relevant for understanding the specific connections between these cell types. To determine which adult dopaminergic mushroom body input neuron types connect to which MBON types, it would be necessary to examine the specific connectivity data held by VFB, such as the upstream and downstream connectivity classes for these neurons.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The [LPLC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fva "Open LPLC2 in Virtual Fly Brain") visual neuron type is a type of neuron in the fly brain with specific characteristics and functions. According to VFB, it has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer (as described by Klapoetke et al., 2017). This arrangement allows it to detect looming (expansion) stimuli (Klapoetke et al., 2017). In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4 (Wu et al., 2016; Tanaka and Clark, 2022). Its arbors span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells (Wu et al., 2016). The LPLC2 neuron projects to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4 (Wu et al., 2016). 

VFB records show that the LPLC2 neuron is connected to various neuron types, including sensory system neurons, visual system neurons, and projection neurons, with 610 downstream class-connectivity partners found. The activity of LPLC2 elicits a jump escape response (Wu et al., 2016; Klapoetke et al., 2017). VFB also indicates that there are approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe (Wu et al., 2016) and they are cholinergic (Davis et al., 2020). 

To further explore the connectivity of LPLC2, you can query VFB for its upstream and downstream connectivity partners. VFB holds data on the neuron types that LPLC2 connects to, which can provide more information on its function and role in the visual system.

results.response: The organisation of the [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") in adult Drosophila has approximately 50 glomeruli, whereas in larval Drosophila it has around 22 glomeruli, as recorded in VFB. VFB holds various data related to the antennal lobe, including images, neurons with different types of terminals, parts and subclasses of the antennal lobe, and tracts/nerves innervating it. results.title: Bidirectional connectivity
results.question: Are there reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons (MBONs) and dopaminergic neurons (DANs)? Which pairs have the strongest mutual connectivity?
results.response:
The connectome data indicates that there are reciprocal connections between mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons. VFB records show 22 reciprocal class-level pairs between these two neuron types. The direction from [dopaminergic neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005131 "Open dopaminergic neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") to [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") has a partner count of 77, while the direction from mushroom body output neuron to dopaminergic neuron has a partner count of 94. The target-to-source weight is 7620 and the source-to-target weight is 2697. 

To identify the specific pairs with the strongest mutual connectivity, one can examine the top partners listed in the VFB findings. VFB holds extensive data on both mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons, including downstream and upstream connectivity classes, which may provide further insights into their connections. For mushroom body output neurons, VFB has annotated [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream connectivity classes and [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes. For dopaminergic neurons, VFB has annotated [8845](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") downstream connectivity classes and [7914](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005131,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for dopaminergic neuron") upstream connectivity classes. 

a narrower follow-up of the specific pairs and their connectivity can be facilitated by exploring the available data on subclasses, transgene expression, and scRNAseq data for both mushroom body output neurons and dopaminergic neurons in VFB.

results.title: Pathway tracing
results.question: Trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. What are the intermediate neuron types and their connections?
results.response:
To trace a pathway from olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn, we can look at the intermediate neuron types and their connections. According to VFB, antennal lobe projection neurons are intermediate neurons that connect olfactory receptor neurons to the lateral horn. The pathway is described as: [olfactory receptor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005926 "Open olfactory receptor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") -> antennal lobe projection neuron -> lateral horn.

VFB holds a significant amount of data related to the [adult lateral horn](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007053 "Open adult lateral horn in Virtual Fly Brain"), including images, neurons with various types of terminals, tracts, and lineage clones. For olfactory receptor neurons, VFB has annotated a large number of images, subclasses, scRNAseq data, transgene expression, and downstream and upstream connectivity classes. 

The connectome data indicates that antennal lobe projection neurons play a key role in this pathway. VFB records show that these neurons have dendrites that innervate the antennal lobe and axons that innervate higher brain centers, including the lateral horn. 

For more detailed information on the specific connections and neuron types involved, you can explore the available VFB data, such as the downstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neurons ([575](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005926,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for olfactory receptor neuron") records) and the neurons with presynaptic or postsynaptic terminals in the adult lateral horn ([816](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in adult lateral horn") and [1375](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00007053,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in adult lateral horn") records, respectively).

results.question: Do the alpha/beta and gamma Kenyon cells converge on any of the same downstream MBON types? Which MBONs receive input from both?
results.response: The connectome data indicates that alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells converge on the same [mushroom body output neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047953 "Open mushroom body output neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") types. VFB records show that some mushroom body output neurons receive input from both alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells. Specifically, VFB found 13 shared downstream target classes among the compared source classes, including mushroom body output neuron 32 and mushroom body output neuron 29. VFB has annotated a large number of connectivity classes for mushroom body output neurons, with [2788](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for MBON") downstream connectivity classes and [2077](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047953,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for MBON") upstream connectivity classes. Additionally, VFB holds a substantial amount of data on the expression patterns and transgene expression for both alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells, as well as scRNAseq data for these cell types. To further investigate the specific mushroom body output neurons that receive input from both alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells, you can explore the downstream connectivity classes for mushroom body output neurons and the upstream connectivity classes for alpha/beta Kenyon cells and gamma Kenyon cells in VFB.

results.title: Anatomical containment chain
results.question: Trace the anatomical containment hierarchy from the DA1 glomerulus up to the top-level brain structure. What is each level in the hierarchy?
results.response:
The containment hierarchy from the [antennal lobe glomerulus DA1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003932 "Open antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 in Virtual Fly Brain") up to the top-level brain structure is: antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 -> adult antennal lobe -> adult deutocerebrum -> adult cerebrum -> adult central brain -> adult brain, as indicated by the VFB data. VFB holds records of neurons and images related to the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, including [10](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, 10 neurons with synaptic terminals in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1, and [911](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003932,ImagesNeurons "Run in VFB: Images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1") images of neurons with some part in antennal lobe glomerulus DA1. 

To further explore the hierarchy, you can query VFB for more information on the adult antennal lobe, adult deutocerebrum, adult cerebrum, adult central brain, and adult brain, as these are the parent structures of the antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 according to the VFB trace containment chain.

results.title: Cross-region connectivity
results.question: What neuron types connect the central complex to the lateral accessory lobe, and how strong are these connections?
results.response:
The neuron types that connect the [adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain") to the [lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00050314 "Open lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018 in Virtual Fly Brain") include larval mushroom body output neurons and larval dopaminergic neurons, specifically [larval mushroom body output neuron f2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047974 "Open larval mushroom body output neuron f2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [larval mushroom body output neuron m1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047988 "Open larval mushroom body output neuron m1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [larval dopaminergic DM1b neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00110928 "Open larval dopaminergic DM1b neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), as recorded in VFB. Additionally, VFB records show that PFL1, PFL2_PB4, PFL3_PB7, PFL1_PB1, PFL1_PB7, and PFL1_PB2 neuron types also connect the central complex to the lateral accessory lobe. 

VFB holds numerous records of neurons with some part in the adult central complex and the lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018, including neurons with synaptic terminals, presynaptic terminals, and postsynaptic terminals. However, the strength of these connections is not specified in the available data. 

To further investigate the connectivity between the adult central complex and the lateral accessory lobe on L3 CNS template, Wood2018, you can explore the available images of neurons with some part in these brain regions, or examine the transgene expression data in the adult central complex.

results.title: Experimental planning
results.question: I want to study the neural circuit underlying CO2 avoidance in Drosophila. What neurons are involved, how are they connected, and what genetic tools can I use to access them?
results.response:
To study the neural circuit underlying CO2 avoidance in Drosophila, you would need to identify the specific neurons involved in this behavior. VFB does not currently hold data on the exact neurons involved in CO2 avoidance. 

The connectome data indicates that several types of sensory neurons are involved in detecting CO2, but VFB has not annotated the specific neural circuit for CO2 avoidance. 

VFB holds records on various genetic tools that can be used to access specific neurons, but without knowing the exact neurons involved in CO2 avoidance, it is difficult to recommend specific tools. 

You can query VFB for neurons that are predicted to be involved in sensory perception or chemosensation, and then explore the available genetic tools for those neurons. 

Follow-up queries can be made to VFB to explore the connectivity of specific neurons, or to find genetic tools that can be used to manipulate or visualize those neurons.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as described by Thomas and Wyman (1984). According to VFB, it has a distinct anatomy and connectivity. 

VFB holds [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") records of images of the giant fiber neuron, specifically DNp01, which can be used to explore its anatomy. Additionally, VFB has annotated [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01, which can provide information on available driver lines for this neuron.

In terms of connectivity, VFB records show that the giant fiber neuron, DNp01, has downstream connectivity classes ([361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records) and upstream connectivity classes ([435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records), indicating its connections with other neurons. 

For further information, relevant publications, such as the one by Thomas and Wyman (1984), can be consulted. VFB also provides a summary of the neuron's profile, including its anatomy, connectivity evidence, genetic tools, and publications, which can be accessed through VFB and VFB functions.

results.title: Hypothesis generation
results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?
results.response: The connectome data indicates that several neuron types might mediate a connection between the [visual system](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047735 "Open visual system in Virtual Fly Brain") and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB records show that neurons such as [ML-VPN2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052139 "Open ML-VPN2 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN1](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052141 "Open Mt-VPN1 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mt-VPN](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052140 "Open Mt-VPN in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Mti](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052142 "Open Mti in Virtual Fly Brain"), [T4ai neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00052241 "Open T4ai neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") have some part in the visual system. Additionally, VFB holds data on adult visual projection neurons that have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body, as described by Vogt et al., 2016. VFB has annotated [1046](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00047735,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in visual system") neurons with some part in the visual system and [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body. The data suggests that visual information could reach the memory circuit via these neurons. VFB holds records of neurons with synaptic terminals, presynaptic terminals, and postsynaptic terminals in both the visual system and the mushroom body, which could be relevant for understanding the connection between these two systems.

results.title: Comparative analysis
results.question: Compare the downstream targets of the two main types of clock neurons (s-LNv and l-LNv). Do they converge on any common target neuron types?
results.response: The downstream targets of [s-LNv](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch03yp "Open s-LNv in Virtual Fly Brain") and [l-LNv](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_jrch0fws "Open l-LNv in Virtual Fly Brain") include several neuron types. According to VFB, the comparison of downstream targets of s-LNv and l-LNv reveals 17 shared downstream target classes, which include adult interneuron, adult cholinergic neuron, adult GABAergic neuron, adult glutamatergic neuron, adult octopaminergic neuron, adult dopaminergic neuron, and adult serotonergic neuron. This suggests that s-LNv and l-LNv converge on common target neuron types, such as adult cholinergic neuron. VFB holds data on these shared downstream targets, which can be further explored to understand the connectivity between s-LNv, l-LNv, and their target neurons.

results.title: Novel circuit exploration
results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
results.response:
The connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") can be explored through the available data in VFB. VFB records show that thermosensory projection neurons relay temperature-detecting neurons to higher brain centers. 

VFB holds downstream connectivity classes for [thermosensory neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005918 "Open thermosensory neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") ([430](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005918,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for thermosensory neuron") records) and upstream connectivity classes for thermosensory neuron ([263](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005918,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for thermosensory neuron") records), which may include connections to or from the mushroom body. Additionally, VFB has annotated neurons with some part in mushroom body ([602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") records), neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body ([599](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in mushroom body") records), neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body ([367](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") records), and neurons with postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body ([301](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPostsynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in mushroom body") records). 

The connectome data indicates potential pathways through which temperature information could influence memory formation, given the role of the mushroom body in memory and learning. However, the specific connection between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body would need to be examined in more detail using the available connectivity data. 

Follow-up queries can be made to explore the specific connections between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body, such as examining the downstream and upstream connectivity classes for thermosensory neuron and the neurons with some part in mushroom body.
